imageAlt: A sample check with numbered callouts.

hotspots.title: 1. Address Field
hotspots.text: Account holder's name, address, phone number, and email address can appear in this section of the check, called the Address Field.

hotspots.title: 2. Bank Information
hotspots.text: The bank name, city and state of the processing facility, or the city and state of the account holder's branch; the bank's phone number; the bank's website address and/or the bank's email address may appear in this section. This section can also be located above field 7 (the memo field).

hotspots.title: 3. Check Number
hotspots.text: The check number appears at the top right, shown here as 101.

hotspots.title: 4. Pay to the Order of
hotspots.text: Pay to the order of. This section should have the name of the person or company that is being paid (the name of the party receiving the check).

hotspots.title: 5. Amount (Numbers)
hotspots.text: The amount written numerically. If this check were for one hundred dollars, within the box labeled "5" in the example above, it should read, "$100.00."

hotspots.title: 6. Amount (Words)
hotspots.text: The amount written in words. If this check were for $100, in the blank section labeled "6," you would write, "One Hundred and 00/100." Many people will then draw a line to the preprinted "Dollars" to discourage alteration. If the check were for $101.59, it would be written, "One Hundred One and 59/100."

hotspots.title: 7. Memo / For
hotspots.text: The "For" or "Memo" section can be left blank, or you can enter any information about the payment. Some people note an account number or invoice number that is being paid with the check, others may just write, "For Birthday" or another note to remind them what the check was for. This field is not read by the bank and does not change how the check is processed.

hotspots.title: 8. Payer Signature
hotspots.text: The signature line. This is where the account holder would sign the check. On a check draft, the signature is not required, although it is common to have a signature disclaimer in this section.

hotspots.title: 9. Routing Number
hotspots.text: This MICR field is the routing number. This is the 9 digit code that routes the check to the issuing bank. The routing number should match the bank name and the fraction code. This number is needed when providing direct deposit information to an employer.

hotspots.title: 10. Account Number
hotspots.text: This is an MICR field that lists the account holder's account number at the bank. This number is also needed when providing direct deposit information to an employer.

hotspots.title: 11. Fraction Code
hotspots.text: Fraction Code. This field is the fraction that denotes the routing for the check. The fraction code is another way to write the 9-digit routing number. If the MICR line on the check is mutilated, the fraction code will be used in its place.

hotspots.title: 12. Date Field
hotspots.text: The date field. Fill this in with the date the check is created
